title: Workload Identity in the cluster: pods without a static key

videos.script: A pod needs to read a bucket. The quick answer is a key file, mounted from a Secret. This lesson is about why that answer is the problem, and what replaces it. {{key}} First, the key. It works from any computer, it never expires, and the Secret holding it is only base64. You will decode one in a single line. {{binding}} Then Workload Identity. The cluster gives each pod's service account a name that Google's IAM understands. A binding says what that name may do. No file exists anywhere. {{token}} Next, the exchange that runs when the pod asks for a token. Five steps, each short-lived, each with its own way of failing. {{direct}} Last, the simplest form. The pod's identity is granted the bucket directly, with no Google service account in between.
